correctness.rationale: For site-dependent SPD matrices, subtracting squared distances yields q(x)=xᵀ(A−B)x+2(Bp)ᵀx−pᵀBp, q(0)<0<q(p). If A−B⪰0 then the 0-cell is a convex quadratic sublevel. Conversely any negative direction of H=A−B gives arbitrarily distant points of C0 along that ray. Star-shapedness from 0 would force the entire ray to lie in C0; negative semidefinite directions by density or the two independent null lines for indefinite H contradict q(p)>0 or force Bp=0. Site exchange gives Cp criterion. If H indefinite, completing square with K=(B⁻¹−A⁻¹)⁻¹ yields hyperbolic phase parameter η=pᵀKp: positive gives disconnected Cp, negative disconnected C0, zero two apex-sharing closed cones. K has inertia (1,1), so η=0 gives exactly two exceptional lines. Haar uniform angles in eigenbasis give 2 arctan(sqrt(μ/λ+))/π for orphan C0, independent of |p|. Independent quadratic phase identities and 200,000-point uniform-angle test gave 0.39183 versus 0.3918265520 for K=diag(2,−1), corroborating rather than proving the general result.
residual_risks: The classification is for two SPD site metrics over the whole plane; clipping or three sites can destroy orphan conclusions.
